text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median 10-session forward return was 0.68%, with a mean of 1.81% and a standard deviation of 8.19%. The single number to anchor on is the 10th percentile of that distribution: -5.81%. This is not a forecast; it is the realised outcome in the worst 10% of matching historical cases over two trading weeks.

[state]
The engine retrieved these specific analogs because KWEB's current state is defined by three extreme features. First, the distance from 52-week high (dist52) is -42.74%, carrying a z-score of -1.899, meaning the ETF is deeply off its highs relative to its own history. Second, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) is -2.663, which maps to a used z-score of -1.607 after clipping, indicating severely depressed liquidity. Third, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, a z-score of 1.124, injecting a macro energy shock into the feature space. Supporting these are a 20-session return (ret20) of -6.97% and a drawdown from the 60-session peak (dd60) of -14.73%. The retrieval weighted name-specific features at 30%, market context at 20%, macro at 20%, crypto at 10%, and event timing at 20%. The closest match sits at a distance of 0.3408, with a median distance across all 50 analogs of 0.4827.

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a median return of 0.68% and a mean of 1.81%. The distribution is heavily right-skewed, with a skew of 2.601, driven by a single massive outlier. The 10th percentile is -5.81%, the 25th percentile is -2.7%, the 75th percentile is 4.69%, and the 90th percentile is 8.66%. In 56% of the analogs, the 10-session return was above zero; in 44%, it was below. The absolute minimum was -9.23% and the maximum was 43.14%. That maximum belongs to NIO on 2025-07-08, which returned 43.14% over 10 sessions and dominates the right tail. The bad tail is populated by recent weakness: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%, HD on 2026-09-03 returned -5.69%, and the closest analog, KWEB itself on 2026-08-31, returned -5.15%. The histogram shows the most frequent bucket is centered at 0.59%, containing 18% of the analogs, while the -5.95% bucket holds 10%.

[tails]
A position can finish near the median and still be un-holdable through the path. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -3.3%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -7.26%, and at the 25th percentile it was -5.96%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, reaching 8.43% at the 75th percentile and 14.31% at the 90th percentile, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.22. Looking at specific drawdown thresholds during the 10 sessions: the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown was 32 out of 50 episodes. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 2 out of 50. No analog breached a 15% or 20% drawdown. The conformal interval, scaled to target 80% coverage, runs from -11.54% to 12.9%, a total width of 24.44%.

[stress]
The stress scenarios reveal how this setup behaved under specific historical regimes. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash is the most severe: using 48 analogs, the median 10-session return was -9.75%, which is -10.43% worse than the baseline median. The 10th percentile was -23.23%, and 47.9% of those episodes fell below -10%. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 75 out of 100. Caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock is directly relevant to China exposure: across 26 analogs, the median return was -3.36% (-4.04% versus baseline), the 10th percentile was -17.57%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 65.4 out of 100. Caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.77% across 36 analogs, with an 11.1% probability of falling below -10% and a 22.2% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2022 inflation/rate bear yielded a median of -4.81% across 50 analogs, with a 30% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median of -3.08% across 50 analogs, with only an 8% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. Conversely, the 2023-03 regional bank stress was benign for this profile: median 4.4% across 36 analogs, with zero probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: very short window; the analog set will be dominated by a handful of sessions. Shock-based scenarios (volatility spike, rates-up, liquidity air pocket, earnings day, FOMC day, crypto contagion, China ADR de-rating) generally produced medians between -1.25% and 0.78%, none materially worse than the baseline except the earnings day shock at -1.25% (caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates). No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the directional hit rate is 49.8%, and the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -2.4%. The PIT chi-square is 306.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the failure of uniformity. Out-of-sample conformal coverage is 83.6% on 2627 queries. Regarding the wrapper: the status is no-verified-wrapper. No Gate.io spot v4 listing passed both verification tests against KWEB, so no wrapper figure is reported for it and none is estimated. The reference market for KWEB is closed for 81.4% of the week (136.67 hours out of 168), meaning any assumption of continuous tradability for this specific ETF is false.
